item.text: I’m checking the current source before changing it again. The next useful refactor is likely in the test and verification path, not the core algorithm, unless I find another structural issue in the sorter itself.

I’m making two focused changes: tightening the core placement loop so each value lookup only happens once, and restructuring the test harness into named cases with a deterministic randomized cross-check against `Arrays.sort`.
The code changes are in. I’m compiling and running the example plus the expanded test harness now to confirm the internal simplification and randomized checks both pass.

Refactored both the core sorter and the test harness.

In [CountingSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/037_counting_sort/CountingSort.java:1), I simplified the stable placement path so each value’s count-table lookup happens once. `sortInPlace(...)` now just delegates to `copyInto(...)`, and `CountingTable.takeOutputIndex(...)` folds the old “read index then decrement” pair into one operation.

In [CountingSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/037_counting_sort/CountingSortTest.java:1), I replaced the flat ad hoc checks with named test methods, added direct coverage for aliased `copyInto(values, values)`, kept wrapper-method coverage, and added a deterministic randomized cross-check against `Arrays.sort`. That makes the repo easier to extend without weakening confidence in the algorithm.
